Apple has updated the privacy policy of the Apple Store app, adding new provisions regarding a virtual shopping assistant that has not yet launched. Details are as follows.

Apple is expanding its use of AI in retail operations

As discovered by MacRumors, the App & Privacy page of the Apple Store app has now added a new section called "Virtual Shopping Assistant" (虛擬購物助理), containing the following content:

In other words, the Apple Store app may soon introduce a chatbot that uses user data to provide personalised suggestions in its responses, helping users make purchasing decisions.

Apple said that before sharing conversation content with unnamed partners providing assistant responses, it will first remove personally identifiable information. This likely means that at least part of the experience will be powered by third-party models from external companies.

Conversation records will be kept within the app for users to review at any time, and will also be retained for Apple's business analytics. Users may separately choose whether to allow conversation content to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant through a new "Chat Improvements" setting.

The wording of Apple's privacy policy suggests that this virtual assistant may initially be available only in certain countries and regions, and may launch first in English-speaking markets before expanding to more languages and regions.

Today's news comes after Apple added an AI chatbot to its "Sales Coach" application several months ago. The "Sales Coach" app provides sales and technical resources for Apple's retail partners. Users can access the chatbot through the "Ask" tab, where it answers questions based on Apple's official training materials and documentation.

Additionally, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple is testing a system called "Live Notes" at some retail stores, which uses AI to record, transcribe, and summarise Genius Bar service interactions, allowing employees to focus on helping customers without being distracted by taking notes.
